name: Tender Collapse
description:
Tender Collapse is the project of neural-composer Mirela Osei-Björk, a Tier 3 artist who began uploading compositions to pirate mesh networks in 2219 under the conceit that all music was co-authored between herself and an unnamed BCI partner she referred to only as 'the listener.' The mechanics were genuine: Osei-Björk composed base structures through extended BCI sessions and then released them as open neural-feed templates that listener-subscribers could modify in real time through their own augmentation, with each listener's neural feedback loop subtly altering the composition's evolution. No two people hear quite the same Tender Collapse piece, and the version a listener hears on first contact is never the version they hear six months later.

The project exists in a legal gray area — Meridian's intellectual property framework has no clear category for music that is partially authored by its listeners' subconscious neural responses — and Osei-Björk has leaned into this ambiguity publicly and with evident relish. The sound is intimate and slightly unsettling: melodic structures from Javanese gamelan tradition broken into microtonal fragments, set against rhythmic patterns drawn from Congolese likembé and processed through what Osei-Björk calls 'scar synthesis' — audio textures designed to feel like something almost remembered. Unaugmented listeners can access a static version through gray-market audio chips, which have become cult objects in Tier 2 and 3 circles.
creator: Mirela Osei-Björk
audience: Augmented Tier 3 experimentalists, gray-market audio chip collectors in Tier 2, BCI-art academics, Tier 4 avant-garde listeners who find Helix Continuum too sterile
cultural_impact: Tender Collapse has quietly reframed the conversation about authorship and identity in GLMZ's music scene. The philosophical question Osei-Björk poses — if your neural responses co-author the music, who owns it, and who are you when you listen? — has migrated from experimental art circles into legal scholarship and BCI ethics debates. Three Vantablack Media subsidiaries have made acquisition offers; Osei-Björk has declined all of them, publicly, in increasingly terse one-sentence statements that have themselves become collectable cultural artifacts distributed on the same gray-market chips as the music.
known_fans: Vantablack Media acquisition scouts who keep being told no
story_hooks: A listener claims that their personal version of a Tender Collapse composition has begun incorporating audio that Osei-Björk insists she never composed — structured sequences that repeat across multiple unconnected listeners' versions, suggesting something is using the neural-feed network as a carrier.

Mirela Osei-Björk has gone dark — no new releases, no mesh presence — three days after a fourth Vantablack Media acquisition offer. Her last gray-market chip contained a composition that, when decoded by a BCI user with the right augmentation profile, plays a sequence of Meridian Security facility access codes.
